chunks: What al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from a man, from Safwan, who said:

I asked al-Rida عليه السلام about a man who left Baghdad wanting to catch up with another man at the distance of one mile, and he continued following him until he reached al-Nahrawan, which is four farsakhs from Baghdad. Should he break his fast if he wants to return, and shorten? He said: He should neither shorten nor break his fast, because he left his home not intending a journey of eight farsakhs. Rather, he only went out intending to catch his companion on part of the road, but the travel continued with him until the place that he reached. But if he had left his home intending al-Nahrawan, going and returning, then he would have had to intend from the night a journey and breaking the fast. If he entered the morning without intending travel, then it appeared to him after morning to travel, he would shorten, but he would not break his fast on that day.

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Rida, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.السَّفَرَ: travel that carries legal consequences for salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting)
key_terms.النَّهْرَوَانَ: the destination mentioned in the case discussed
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةَ فَرَاسِخَ: the legal travel distance of eight farsakhs in this ruling
key_terms.مِنَ اللَّيْلِ: from the night, indicating prior intention before dawn
key_terms.يَنْوِيَ: to form the intention for travel
key_terms.يُفْطِرُ: to break the sawm (fast) while traveling
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: to shorten the four-unit salat (prayer) during travel

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler shorten salat (prayer) and break the fast according to intention of travel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on shortening salat (prayer) and breaking the fast during travel based on the traveler's intention at the time of departure. If one did not initially intend the full legal travel distance, he does not break his fast or shorten salat (prayer), even if the journey later extends; but if travel is decided after dawn, he shortens salat (prayer) without breaking that day's fast.
